text: What is the function of the Shine-Dalgarno (SD) sequence within a bacterial ribosome binding site (RBS)?
choices: It forms a stable stem-loop structure that halts RNA polymerase, terminating transcription
It binds the σ70 subunit of RNA polymerase to initiate transcription at the correct start site
It is cleaved by a self-cleaving ribozyme to create a defined mRNA 5' end independent of upstream sequence
It base-pairs with the complementary anti-SD sequence at the 3' end of the 16S rRNA, recruiting the ribosome to the start codon
explanation: The Shine-Dalgarno sequence base-pairs with the complementary anti-SD sequence at the 3' end of 16S rRNA, positioning the ribosome so it can locate the downstream start codon and begin translation. Choice 0 describes an intrinsic transcriptional terminator, a different genetic part acting on RNA polymerase rather than the ribosome. Choice 1 describes promoter/sigma-factor function during transcription initiation, and choice 2 describes a ribozyme-based insulator (such as RiboJ), which acts on the mRNA 5' end rather than mediating ribosome recruitment.
